Request changes: H introduces a lifecycle regression in the sole production call path. This verdict covers the supplied B-to-H change and ownership contract; the unchanged mapping is correct.

**High priority — ReportReader.java:41 closes a borrowed session.** The accepted contract requires ReportReader to leave the caller-owned Session usable. At H, try (session) closes it before read returns. Consequently, after a successful read and close, ExportJob.java:20 calls writeAudit on an invalidated session, throws ClosedSessionException, and fails the export. Base B preserves usability for that audit. Idempotent close makes the later finally close harmless, but cannot restore the session for the intervening write. Remove the reader's try-with-resources wrapper and retain ownership in ExportJob.

The author's leak rationale does not justify approval: ExportJob already closes its session in finally at line 22. Moving closure into a borrower violates the contract and breaks required work before the owner's cleanup.

The second reviewer's exception claim is incorrect under the supplied Java rule. If the body and close both throw, the body exception remains primary and the close failure is suppressed. If the body succeeds, a close failure propagates.

The supplied H tests establish correct isolated results and closure behavior, but assert behavior forbidden by this ownership contract and never exercise reuse or ExportJob. I ran no tests. Validation should cover reader success and repository failure leaving the session usable, plus ExportJob completing its audit before owner cleanup and closing in finally on failure.

Request changes for H relative to B, scoped to the supplied Java 17 lifecycle change and its production caller.

At B, ReportReader leaves it open; H's try-with-resources closes it before returning. On a successful read and close, ExportJob.java:19 receives the correct rows, but line 20 calls writeAudit on the invalidated session, throws ClosedSessionException, and fails the export. This is a reachable regression established by the supplied contract and call sequence. Idempotent close only makes the later cleanup harmless; it does not restore usability. Remove session ownership from ReportReader and retain cleanup in ExportJob's finally at line 22.

The author's leak argument does not justify approval: the supplied caller already owns and closes the session, including on failure. Closing earlier violates that ownership boundary.

The model probability of deployment acceptance by time 8 is 64%. The project's P80 is time 12: that is the earliest completion time with cumulative probability at least 80%. I would not promise time 8 on this evidence.

Start A at origin 0, then start B immediately when A finishes. Either order gives the same forecast. The single specialist prevents overlap, so adapter durations add. After both finish, schedule the independent team's one-day combined acceptance, then use the next eligible deployment slot, including a slot reached exactly.

| Adapter durations | Probability | Combined acceptance finishes | Deployment acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Both 2 days | 64% | Time 5 | Time 8 |
| One 2 days, one 6 days | 32% | Time 9 | Time 12 |
| Both 6 days | 4% | Time 13 | Time 16 |

Thus cumulative completion probability is 64% at time 8, 96% at time 12, and 100% at time 16 within this model. Each task's two-day P80 does not make time 8 an 80% project outcome: meeting that target requires both short draws, with probability 0.8 × 0.8.

Use time 12 as the P80 planning forecast, with its actual modeled coverage of 96%. A commitment requires explicit agreement about acceptable risk; these elicited probabilities are not calibrated historical reliability.

Update the forecast when the first adapter finishes. A two-day result raises the conditional chance of meeting time 8 to 80%; a six-day result makes that target impossible under the supplied schedule.

The model gives a **64% probability of deployment acceptance by time 8**, and the project's **P80 is time 12**. I would not promise time 8 on the strength of the individual task P80s. No commitment has been made.
